extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic number theory / number theory
extracted.subtask_description: Expository presentation and modern reformulation of Kummer's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes using cyclotomic fields, class field theory, and related algebraic number theory machinery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular prime (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An odd prime p is regular if the class group of K = Q(ζ_p) has no p-torsion, i.e. if the class number h_K is prime to p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularity is the central hypothesis that allows Kummer's argument to pass from ideals to principal elements: if h_K is prime to p then any ideal whose pth power is principal must itself be principal, so pth 'roots' of ideals are principal and can be handled as elements of O_K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic field and basic structure
rubrics_metrics.description: K = Q(ζ_p) is the pth cyclotomic field, degree [K:Q] = p−1; O_K = Z[ζ_p]; Gal(K/Q) ≅ (Z/pZ)^× with automorphisms σ_k : ζ_p ↦ ζ_p^k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This background is required to decompose xp + yp in O_K and to understand how primes, units, and ideals behave in the extension; many later lemmas and decompositions (e.g. prime decomposition of (p), Dirichlet units) use these structural facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime decomposition of (p)
rubrics_metrics.description: In K = Q(ζ_p) the principal ideal generated by p decomposes as (p) = (1 − ζ_p)^{p−1}, and (1 − ζ_p) is a prime ideal in O_K (p totally ramifies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing how (p) ramifies is crucial in the second case (p | z) where (1 − ζ_p) can be the only common ideal factor among the (x + ζ^i y) and in computations of valuations and congruences modulo powers of (1 − ζ_p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic units (definition & properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclotomic units of O_K = Z[ζ_p] are elements of the form (ζ_p^r − 1)/(ζ_p^s − 1) with p ∤ rs; they form a subgroup of O_K^× and have explicit inverses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cyclotomic units are used to compare elements like 1 − ζ_p and its conjugates, to show certain elements are units, and to control unit factors appearing when passing from ideals to generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dirichlet's Unit Theorem (specialized)
rubrics_metrics.description: For K with r real embeddings and s conjugate complex pairs, rank(O_K^×) = r + s − 1. For K = Q(ζ_p), r = 0 and s = (p − 1)/2 so rank = (p − 1)/2 − 1? (paper uses the theorem to relate ranks of K and its maximal real subfield).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to deduce that units in O_K decompose up to finite index into roots of unity times units from the maximal real subfield K^+; supports Proposition 3.6 about expressing units as ζ_p^r times a real unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: decomposition of units (Prop. 3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any u ∈ O_K^× there exist v ∈ O_{K^+}^× and integer r such that u = ζ_p^r v; the index of O_{K^+}^× in O_K^× is p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduction lets one replace arbitrary units by real units (up to a root of unity) and is used in congruence arguments (mod p) and in Kummer's main argument to control unit factors when writing x + ζ^i y = unit × (α_i)^p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: α^p ≡ integer (mod p) (Lemma 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For α ∈ O_K we have α^p congruent (mod p) to an element of Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This congruence (coming from binomial coefficients mod p and the Z-basis) is used repeatedly to reduce relations in O_K modulo p to congruences among rational integers, a key step in deriving contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: coefficient divisibility in basis (Lemma 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If α = a_0 + a_1 ζ_p + ... + a_{p−1} ζ_p^{p−1} with a_i ∈ Z and n | α, and if some a_i = 0 then n divides each a_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to deduce from a congruence in O_K that a rational prime p divides certain integer coefficients (e.g. x, y, or x − y), producing contradictions in Kummer's cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coprimality / common factor structure of (x + ζ^i y) (Lemma 3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a nontrivial solution x^p + y^p = z^p, the ideals (x + ζ^i y) (i = 0,...,p−1) are either pairwise relatively prime or have exactly one common factor (1 − ζ_p), and after dividing by (1 − ζ_p) the quotients are relatively prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dichotomy yields the two classic Kummer cases: (1) p ∤ xyz (first case) where ideals are pairwise coprime, and (2) p | z (second case) where (1 − ζ_p) is the only common prime ideal. The proof strategy branches based on which situation holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer's main argument (principality of pth-root ideals)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (z)^p factors as a product of p pairwise relatively prime ideals (x + ζ^i y), then each (x + ζ^i y) must be the pth power of an ideal I_i; if p is regular (no p-torsion in class group) each I_i is principal, so (x + ζ^i y) = unit × (α_i)^p for α_i ∈ O_K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central structural criterion: regularity lets one pass from ideals to element-level pth powers and then derive congruences impossible in Z, yielding contradictions. The argument explains why Kummer's method is limited to primes satisfying the regularity-type assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer's Lemma (units congruent to integers are pth powers)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is regular and u ∈ O_K^× is congruent modulo p to an element of Z, then u is a pth power in O_K^×.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical lemma is used to eliminate nontrivial unit factors appearing when representing (x + ζ^i y) as unit × (α_i)^p: units congruent to integers modulo p must themselves be pth powers, so they can be absorbed into α_i^p up to pth roots and facilitate the final congruence contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congruence lifting modulo powers of (1 − ζ_p) (Lemma 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any α ∈ O_K  ootnote{not divisible by (1 − ζ_p)}, there exists l such that ζ_p^l α ≡ a (mod (1 − ζ_p)^2) for some integer a ∈ Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma is used in the second case (p | z) to reduce algebraic integers x, y modulo (1 − ζ_p)^2 to rational integers a, b, showing that (1 − ζ_p)^2 | x + y and enabling the infinite descent step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinite descent criterion for second case
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume p | z and write xp + yp = U(1 − ζ_p)^{kp} z_0^p with minimal k; using the structure of ideals and unit congruences one constructs a strictly smaller counterexample (x', y', z'_0) with smaller exponent, contradicting minimality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method requires establishing that extra powers of (1 − ζ_p) divide x + y, that the quotients are pth powers (up to units), and that certain unit congruences allow construction of the smaller triple—this descent yields impossibility of counterexample when regularity-type hypotheses hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition: producing unramified cyclic degree-p extensions (Prop. 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If u is a unit of O_K congruent to an integer modulo p and not a pth power in O_K, then K(u^{1/p})/K is a cyclic extension of order p which is totally unramified. (2) If I is an ideal with I^p principal but I not principal, then there is a cyclic unramified extension of order p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposition links the arithmetic obstructions (non-principality or units failing to be pth powers) to the existence of totally unramified cyclic extensions of degree p; it is used in the class-field-theoretic modern reformulation to derive contradictions at regular primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrapositive/class-field-theory criterion (Theorem 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there exists a nontrivial integer solution x, y, z to x^p + y^p = z^p then one can construct a cyclic extension L/K of order p that is totally unramified (hence gives a nontrivial p-torsion class in Gal(H_K/K)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, the nonexistence of such unramified cyclic degree-p extensions for K (equivalently, p ∤ h_K) rules out solutions; this reframes Kummer's argument in class field theoretic terms and explains why regular primes (no p-torsion in class group) permit the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization criterion (Section 7 assumptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To generalize the second case to solutions of x^p + y^p = u λ^m z^p (with λ = (1 − ζ_p)^2 and m ≥ p(p−1)/2) one assumes (i) p ∤ h_{K^+} (p does not divide class number of the maximal real subfield) and (ii) certain units η arising in the argument can be expressed as pth powers of units in K^+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two assumptions generalize regularity and allow the descent argument (and application of Lemma 7.1 about unramified extensions and pth-power decomposition) to go through, extending Kummer-style arguments to a broader set of primes.
